reading: Two single cells sit on the long edges. Each becomes a full line across the short dimension, and the pair of lines repeats toward the far end with period twice their spacing, colours alternating.

slots.seeds: the two marker cells (first and second along the long axis)
slots.orientation: lines run across the short dimension of the grid
slots.period: 2 x distance between the two seeds
slots.colours: alternate the two seed colours, starting at the first seed and continuing to the far border

why: every output line lies at seed1 + k*d along the long axis (d = seed spacing), coloured seed1 for even k and seed2 for odd k; nothing before seed1
invariants: cells before the first seed stay background

reading: Each red (2) cell gets yellow (4) on its four diagonal neighbours; each blue (1) cell gets orange (7) on its four orthogonal neighbours. Other colours get nothing.

new_rows.name: red_diag
new_rows.datalog: red_diag(Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, 2), off(DY, DX), Q = DY*DY + DX*DX, Q = 2, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, B).

new_rows.name: blue_orth
new_rows.datalog: blue_orth(Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, 1), off(DY, DX), Q = DY*DY + DX*DX, Q = 1, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, B).

why: diagonal neighbours of every 2 are 4 (first fill, colour 4); orthogonal neighbours of every 1 are 7 (second fill, colour 7); markers themselves and other colours unchanged
invariants: all input cells keep their colour

reading: A fixed colour substitution applied to every cell: 1<->5, 2<->6, 3<->4, 8<->9.
why: each cell of colour a becomes key(a) with key = {1:5,5:1,2:6,6:2,3:4,4:3,8:9,9:8}, the same on all pairs

reading: Pairs of blue (1) cells on opposite borders are joined by a full blue line; every red (2) rectangle that the line passes through turns entirely blue.

new_rows.name: paint
new_rows.datalog:
vline(X) :- cell(Y1, X, 1), cell(Y2, X, 1), Y2 > Y1.
hline(Y) :- cell(Y, X1, 1), cell(Y, X2, 1), X2 > X1.
online(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), vline(X).
online(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), hline(Y).
hit(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, 2), online(Y, X).
paint(Y, X) :- online(Y, X).
paint(Y, X) :- hit(O), obj(O, Y, X).

why: the region (lines between same-row/same-column 1-pairs plus every 2-object they touch) is all 1 (colour 1); everything else unchanged
invariants: red rectangles not on a line

reading: Each single cell becomes a full horizontal line of its colour; the grid's left and right border columns are coloured by the nearest marker row (ties go to the upper marker), and the top/bottom rows take the colour of the first/last marker.

slots.lines: full row through each marker in its colour
slots.bands: each row belongs to the marker with nearest row (tie -> upper); its two border cells get that colour
slots.caps: top row filled with the first marker's colour, bottom row with the last marker's colour

why: every non-background output cell is on a marker row, on the left/right border (nearest-marker colour), or on the top/bottom row

reading: A small multicoloured key pattern is rotated 90 degrees clockwise and scaled up to fit the large grey (8) silhouette; each block of the silhouette takes the colour of the corresponding key cell.

slots.transform: rotate key 90 degrees clockwise, scale by target_size / key_size (3 in pair 0, 2 in pair 1)
slots.paint: each target block coloured with the rotated key cell's colour

why: the 8-object's cells partition into k x k blocks aligned with the rotated key; block colour = key cell colour; the key stays

reading: The input is tiled 2x2, then every background cell diagonally adjacent to a coloured cell becomes azure (8).

new_rows.name: diag_bg
new_rows.datalog:
isfg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
diag_bg(Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Q = DY*DY + DX*DX, Q = 2, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, B), !isfg(Y2, X2).

why: output = 2x2 tiling of the input with all background diagonal neighbours of foreground cells set to 8 (no wraparound)
invariants: original coloured cells in every tile copy

reading: Three cells mark three corners of a rectangle. A grey (5) cell is placed at the rectangle's centre, and each corner's colour is placed one diagonal step from the centre toward that corner.

slots.corners: the three marker cells (bounding box gives the rectangle)
slots.centre: centre cell of the bounding box, coloured 5
slots.copies: for each corner, its colour at centre + (sign(dy), sign(dx)) toward it

why: exactly four new cells: 5 at the box centre, and each marker colour at the diagonal neighbour of the centre in that marker's direction

reading: Every 4-connected single-colour component with fewer than 3 cells is recoloured green (3); larger components stay.

new_rows.name: small4
new_rows.datalog:
adj4(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Q = DY*DY + DX*DX, Q = 1, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
reach(Y, X, Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
reach(Y, X, Y3, X3) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2), adj4(Y2, X2, Y3, X3).
csize(Y, X, count(Y2, X2)) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2).
small4(Y, X) :- csize(Y, X, N), N < 3.

why: cells in 4-connected components of size 1 or 2 become 3 (key 1,5,7,8 -> 3); all other cells unchanged

reading: A full grey (5) wall lies on one border. Each coloured segment sweeps toward the wall, each cell drawing a line of its own colour that stops at the first non-background cell (another segment or the wall).
why: from every segment cell, a line in the direction of the wall covers exactly the background cells up to the first obstacle; the wall itself is not a source
invariants: cells behind segments (away from the wall)
